results.title: VanEck GDX Index Review May Generate $43 million Inflow to AMMN, $37 million to BRMS, and $3 million to ARCI
results.body: The upcoming VanEck Gold Miners (GDX) index evaluation, effective 18 September 2026, raises the free‑float ratios of PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk from 21 % to 26 %, PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk from 51 % to 60 %, and PT Archi Indonesia Tbk from 10 % to 16 %, increasing their index weights. Stockbit analyst Theodorus Melvin projects passive foreign fund inflows of US$43 million into AMMN, US$37 million into BRMS, and US$3 million into ARCI. In contrast, PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk’s free‑float fell to 31 % and is expected to see an outflow of about US$18 million, while PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk, with a stable 10 % free‑float, may face an outflow of US$0.2 million. The free‑float changes are linked to a Hong Kong IPO and a share purchase by PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk, and the next GDX review will be announced on 11 December 2026 (effective 18 December 2026) with the GDXJ review slated for around March 2027.

results.title: IHSG Opens Weaker at Start of Week, Pressured by Global Sentiment
results.body: The IHSG opened 1.36% lower at 6,452 on Monday as rising oil prices above $100 per barrel and an 85% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting pressured sentiment. Foreign investors sold a net Rp2.31 trillion in the regular market, while trading volume reached 6.53 billion shares worth Rp3.06 trillion. Technical indicators show a hammer pattern at the 6,475-6,375 support zone with the index holding above its 20-day moving average at 6,533, suggesting a potential rebound. Brokerages offered divergent outlooks: BRI Danareksa sees a constructive bias targeting resistance at 6,600-6,700 and favors UNTR, IMPC, and TINS; Phintraco expects sideways movement between 6,450-6,700 and picks ANTM, ASII, EMAS, MDKA, and ISAT; CGS International forecasts varied gains with support at 6,465-6,390 and resistance at 6,620-6,695, recommending TAPG, AALI, ISAT, TINS, AMMN, and EMAS; Panin Sekuritas anticipates further weakness due to geopolitical tensions and foreign outflows, selecting INET, BRMS, and INCO.

results.title: Grup Djarum, Low Tuck Kwong, and Prajogo Pangestu Stocks Weigh Down the IHSG for the Week
results.body: During the week of 7–11 September 2026, shares of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bayan Resources Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk, and PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk fell sharply, delivering the largest negative contributions to the IHSG, with BBCA down 5.60% (‑33.09 points), BYAN down 10.51% (‑23.63 points), BBRI down 3.54% (‑17.51 points), DSSA down 6.78% (‑6.86 points), BBNI down 4.82% (‑6.26 points), BRMS down 5.59% (‑5.95 points), BRPT down 5.03% (‑5.22 points), BMRI down 1.36% (‑4.90 points), BREN down 3.57% (‑4.64 points), and VKTR down 8.09% (‑4.31 points). The composite index slipped 1.43% to 6,541,377, while total market capitalization fell 1.32% to Rp11,446 trillion and average daily transaction value dropped 14.88% to Rp16.36 trillion. Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp690.19 billion on 11 September, contributing to a year‑to‑date net outflow of Rp71,415 trillion.

results.title: IHSG Falls 1.49% in First Session as Global Markets Slide on Oil Surge and Fed Rate Hike Bets
results.body: The Indonesian Composite Stock Price Index (IHSG) fell 1.49% to 6,490 in the first trading session on Friday, driven by heavy selling pressure across the market. Big-cap stocks BYAN, BBCA, and BRMS were the primary weights on the index, while transport, non-primary consumer, and infrastructure sectors led declines of more than 1.7% each. The selloff tracked a broad decline across Asian markets as Brent crude surged above $108 per barrel and stronger-than-expected US producer inflation increased the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike to 70%. The rupiah weakened to 17,610 per US dollar amid dollar strength fueled by rate hike expectations. Panin Sekuritas cited escalating geopolitical tensions, oil above $100 per barrel, and heavy foreign outflows as key drivers.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily bought BBRI shares and sold CPIN and BRMS in the week of August 31–September 4, 2026.
results.body: Foreign investor trading activity in Indonesian stocks for the week of August 31–September 4, 2026 showed net buying overall, with the IHSG rising 1.82% to 6,636.47. Foreign investors recorded a net buy of Rp2.3 trillion across the market, reducing the year-to-date net sell in the regular market to Rp96.11 trillion. The largest net buy was in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp1.43 trillion, driving its share price up 6.27% to Rp3,390. The largest net sell was in PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk at Rp516.62 billion, though its share price still rose 4.91% to Rp3,210. BRMS also saw significant foreign selling, according to the report.

results.title: Foreign Investors Return to Bumi Resources (BUMI) as Samuel Sekuritas Maintains Buy Rating with Rp 300 Target
results.body: Foreign investors reversed course to become net buyers of Bumi Resources (BUMI) shares, recording a net buy of Rp 83.2 billion during August 31–September 4, 2026, after a net sell of Rp 132.1 billion the prior week. The stock closed at Rp 210 on September 4, up 1.9% daily and 10.5% weekly, though still down 42.6% year-to-date. Samuel Sekuritas reiterated a buy recommendation with a Rp 300 target price, implying 42.8% upside, based on a sum-of-the-parts valuation that factors in stronger third-quarter 2026 performance driven by the Wolfram gold mine ramp-up, earnings recovery at subsidiary Bumi Resources Minerals (BRMS), lower fuel costs, and potential coal price gains from El Niño. The broker also flagged risks including near-term coal price weakness, acquisition execution delays, slower Wolfram production growth, and gold price declines.

results.title: The Fate of Indonesian Stocks Amid MSCI's Whirlwind
results.body: MSCI Inc’s August 2026 index review, effective 1 September, removed GOTO and CPIN from the MSCI Global Standard, leaving nine Indonesian constituents: UNTR, BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BRMS, BBRI, BRPT, ASII and TLKM. During 1-2 September, foreign investors net bought the five most sought-after stocks—BBRI (Rp 993.29 bn), BBCA (Rp 589.83 bn), BMRI (Rp 227.78 bn), BBNI (Rp 36.34 bn) and BRPT (Rp 43.86 bn)—while net selling UNTR (Rp 10.11 bn), BRMS (Rp 54.06 bn), TLKM (Rp 111.7 bn) and ASII (Rp 65.92 bn). On the latest trading day, BBRI rose 0.30% to Rp 3,390, BBCA jumped 1.14% to Rp 6,675, BMRI gained 0.93% to Rp 4,360, BBNI climbed 0.78% to Rp 3,900 and BRPT slipped 0.55% to Rp 1,820, while ASII fell 1.63% to Rp 4,840, TLKM dropped 0.77% to Rp 2,590, BRMS declined 1.37% to Rp 720 and UNTR slipped 2.05% to Rp 25,050. The divergent net foreign flows underscore varying investor sentiment among the remaining MSCI constituents after the index composition change.

results.title: Review the Stock Recommendations for PWON, SILO, and BRMS for Thursday Trading (3/9/2026)
results.body: PT Pakuwon Jati Tbk (PWON), PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO), and PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) are the three Indonesian companies whose shares receive trading recommendations for Thursday, 3 September 2026. PWON is advised to buy on weakness with support at Rp 258 and resistance at Rp 290, after closing at Rp 272, down 1.45% on 2 September. SILO receives a wait‑and‑see recommendation with support at Rp 2,110 and resistance at Rp 2,210, after closing at Rp 2,160, up 1.41% on 2 September.
